source_snapshot.test_name_items: Upgrade and Downgrade DCSCM-CPLD firmware by Redfish when system is booted
source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Upgrade / Downgrade FPGA firmware through redfish.
1. Enter the command on the command line to set the behavior of BMC after update.
Command : curl -k -X PATCH https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/ -H "Content-Type:application/json" -d '{"HttpPushUriOptions":{"HttpPushUriApplyTime":{"ApplyTime": "Immediate"}}}'
2. Change the name of the firmware file to be updated in the green text. This command may take some time to upload the firmware to BMC.
Command : curl -k -X POST https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/update -H "Content-Type:application/octet-stream" --data-binary @${File_name}
3. Waiting for the flash progress complete.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
Firmware should be flashed successfully after BMC reset only one time.
curl -k -X GET https://root:0penBmc@${BMC_IP}/redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: curl (Redfish REST client, on the BMC side) + DCSCM-CPLD image (user provides)
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- DCSCM-CPLD downgrade via Redfish (system is booted): the agent needs the exact user-provided DCSCM-CPLD image first the SUT must be booted first and the host OS running for the flash, then runs the Redfish update flow: `PATCH /redfish/v1/UpdateService` (set preserve/replace behavior), `POST /redfish/v1/UpdateService` to upload the image, poll the returned TaskService task to completion, then `GET /redfish/v1/UpdateService/FirmwareInventory` to confirm the new version is active. Not a single one-liner; run step-by-step after the image is placed on the BMC.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the full Redfish PATCH/POST response, the TaskService poll loop, and the final `FirmwareInventory` JSON so the user confirms the DCSCM-CPLD version changed, only one BMC reset happened, and the SUT still boots/passes self-checks.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: DCSCM-CPLD firmware flash via Redfish is state-changing and can brick the BMC/host if interrupted; flash only the user-specified image with host powered off for a clean result, and never interrupt mid-flash.

original_test_intent: The row appears intended to exercise a DCSCM-CPLD Redfish upgrade/downgrade while booted, yet its operative Procedure names FPGA, leaving the destructive device target undefined.
original_method: PATCH Immediate apply, POST an image to the assumed update URI, wait, perform an undefined sole BMC reset and read generic FirmwareInventory; no component selector is stated.
manual_activity: Platform/RD must identify the programmable device and its recovery ownership; an authorized engineer approves the corrected high-risk update/reset plan.
required_inputs: Master-source correction selecting DCSCM-CPLD or FPGA
Exact board/device identity and signed transition images
Secret/TLS policy and DCSCM/BMC recovery path
safety_requirements: Do not upload an image to generic UpdateService while the hardware target is contradictory and no component selector is defined.
Do not expose the BMC root secret or disable certificate validation in the approved flow.
Do not reset or power-cycle to force activation after an ambiguous response; retain task and SEL evidence.
Require a recovery route that remains available if the DCSCM management/control plane fails.
agent_execution_scope: After correction, discover component-specific capabilities, verify signed image binding and run one approved transition with deterministic task/reset tracking.
No firmware POST, PATCH or BMC reset is permitted while target and state semantics remain unresolved; no formal verdict is set.
engineer_actions: Correct Items/Procedure consistency and define DCSCM-specific activation/readback.
Approve image, host/reset, security and alternate-recovery plan; judge results.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: DCSCM-CPLD matches Items and Script, but not the source Procedure; generic FirmwareInventory/task polling does not prove the intended device was selected.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Withhold all writes. After source correction, use only a vendor-advertised action that explicitly binds the image to the corrected component and returns auditable activation status.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The DCSCM Items/FPGA Procedure mismatch, supplied PATCH/POST/GET, booted condition, 10/30-minute values and one-reset criterion remain.

modernized_recommendation.status: PENDING DCSCM TARGET AND RECOVERY CONTRACT
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Correct and uniquely identify the programmable device, validate a signed image against the DCSCM board revision, invoke a component-bound vendor action, account for the approved BMC reset and verify DCSCM inventory plus BMC/host recovery independently.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only a corrected DCSCM-CPLD platform whose Redfish service advertises the required target/action.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record Redfish schema, BMC release, DCSCM hardware/CPLD image and client versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor DCSCM-CPLD programming, activation and rescue documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds a component selector and alternate management recovery while removing embedded credentials and assumed endpoints.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Proves the DCSCM device—not an FPGA or other inventory member—was updated and management survived activation.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Source correction plus vendor target/action contract.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Loss of DCSCM logic may remove the normal management path, so recovery cannot depend solely on the updated device.

project_override_considerations: A project can supply DCSCM versions and a vendor action only after the Master source chooses the target; overrides cannot silently reinterpret FPGA as DCSCM-CPLD.
expected_evidence: Approved component correction and DCSCM board identity
Advertised component selector/action and redacted terminal task evidence
Post-update DCSCM inventory, BMC reachability, host boot and SEL
Independent recovery readiness and engineer verdicts

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items and Script target DCSCM-CPLD; Procedure explicitly instructs FPGA firmware. The same row also says booted while its risk says powered off, and the criterion's sole BMC reset is undefined.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The hardware destination of a destructive image is not an ordinary project parameter and cannot be guessed. Together with incompatible host/reset state, it prevents a safe executable plan.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Its DCSCM interpretation is retained only as historical evidence, not adopted as a source rewrite.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: BLOCKED is retained, now tied directly to component identity and DCSCM recovery blast radius.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Avoids treating missing images as the blocker; the actual block is contradictory destructive target/state semantics.

review_improvement: Requires auditable device selection and an alternate recovery path suitable for a management-module CPLD.
independent_technical_reasoning: A generic UpdateService POST cannot safely resolve which firmware inventory member receives the payload. Because DCSCM-CPLD and FPGA are materially different recovery domains, the source conflict must be corrected before automation classification can be reassessed.
